sets.title: Law and method changes
sets.what: Changes since 2016 that break year-to-year comparisons.
rows: SB 202: absentee applications accepted 78 to 11 days before the election (was 180 days to the Friday before); ID number required on applications and ballots; no unsolicited application mailings by officials.
Mail volumes and timing in 2022-2026 not comparable to 2016-2020 (2020 also had the statewide application mailing).
SB 202: drop boxes only inside early-voting sites during advance-voting hours, capped by county population.
SB 202: advance voting weekdays 9-5 minimum plus mandatory second and third Saturdays; Sundays optional. Advance voting starts the fourth Monday before the election (2026: Oct 13 to Fri Oct 30).
2016/2018 already had 3 weeks of advance voting; 2022-2026 add a mandatory second Saturday.
SB 202: officials may open outer envelopes and scan absentee ballots from 8:00 a.m. on the third Monday before the election; tabulation results not released before polls close.
Absentee results arrive early on election night in 2022-2026 (2020 had slow absentee counts in some counties).

SB 189 (2024): counties must report all early in-person and absentee ballots received by election day within hours of polls closing (target by 8 p.m.); QR-code ballot changes deferred; voter-challenge rules.
Faster first returns than 2022; reporting order: early and absentee first.
R (bill page JS-rendered; text not opened)
Absentee ballots must be received by 7 p.m. Election Day (UOCAVA: postmarked by ED, received within 3 days).
Court-ordered remedial congressional and legislative maps enacted Dec 2023, used in 2024 and 2026.
2026 CD/SD/HD = 2024 lines; 2022 and earlier are different lines.
County superintendents certify consolidated returns by 5:00 p.m. on the Monday following the election (SB 202 changed this from the second Friday): Mon Nov 9, 2026.
registration rolls grow; turnout-of-registered falls without a turnout change; breaks every comparison year before 2016
